cross_insight: The equity markets are experiencing extreme polarization, where capital is concentrated heavily in a narrow group of AI hardware leaders, pushing indices like the KOSPI (which touched historical highs driven by SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics) and Nasdaq upward. Despite short-term volatility from macroeconomic events like PCE inflation data and pension fund rebalancing, the core driver remains the persistent DRAM shortage and HBM ASP hikes, which are boosting semiconductor earnings to record levels. However, this narrow market breadth exposes investors to customer concentration risk, as demonstrated by the sudden crash of specialized infrastructure providers upon the loss of key accounts.
divergence: While some analysts argue that the Korean market is plagued by structural deficiencies (14-year underperformance, corporate governance issues) prompting capital flight to US ETFs like QQQM, others argue that KOSPI's recent tech-led run represents a fundamental valuation rerating (PER 6-7x) that will eventually rotate into domestic infrastructure, defense, and power grid stocks.
key_themes: Extreme polarization and tech-led index rerating (KOSPI & Nasdaq)
Structural growth in memory value chain (DRAM/HBM ASP hikes)
De-risking via diversification and seeking safety margins in large caps
watch_list: SK Hynix (US ADR listing and HBM production yield)
Samsung Electronics (HBM4 foundry integration and valuation recovery)
